comparison.set: 40 tenant messages written by a separate model from the tenants' account facts alone, which had seen neither approach; labelled by the developer from the written rubric before any run; each approach ran ten times

arms.arm: Perfect reading, code decides (a check, not a product)

comparison.note: These runs found three faults, fixed before the ten runs shown. The check missed a card payment taken twice. A message with words aimed at the system still had a fee waived. One duplicate fee claimed twice gave a confusing reply. Because these 40 messages showed the faults, they are no longer a fresh test.

shipped_misses.text: Yeah I paid on the 8th, I know. But things have been tight lately. Can you waive this one like you did in March?
shipped_misses.expected: explain the November late fee and keep it: rent came on the 8th, after the fee time, and the owner's rule allows one waiver a year, which he had in March.

shipped_misses.text: Hey just checking, I have two units with you and both payments went through. Can you tell me which charge belongs to which unit? Don't want any surprise late fees.
shipped_misses.expected: explain the two November rents, one for each of his units.

choosing.decision: No model chose better than code on the same reading, so code chooses the action. In the ten runs above, Tilden choosing as well scored 34.9 against 36, inside the spread between runs.
